newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH LAWMAKERS WANT TO RAISE VAT ON FAST FOOD.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH LAWMAKERS WANT TO RAISE VAT ON FAST FOOD.

text.p: French lawmakers have proposed a higher tax on fast food, nicknamed the "Big Mac tax", to protect the old-fashioned French bistrot and raise revenue.
The National Assembly's finance committee adopted an amendment to the 1997 budget raising the rate of Value Added Tax (VAT) charged on take-away food from 5.5 to 20.6 percent.
Parliamentarians have nicknamed it the "Big Mac tax" because it would hit U.S. hamburger giant McDonalds Corp .
"This fast-food amendment is not just aimed at hamburgers," committee chairman Pierre Mehaignerie told reporters. "It will also hit sandwich vendors and other take-away outlets."
He calculated that the increase, if adopted in the final budget, would yield up to one billion francs ($193 million) in extra revenue.

The amendment follows pressure from cafe and restaurant owners who complain they face unfair competition because they have to charge the full rate of VAT on food and drink served, while fast-food outlets, which have exploded in number in the last decade, pay the lower rate charged on retail food.
The full assembly will consider the budget from next week. The government has the power to override amendments but has not yet said what it will do about the fast-food tax.
